cards.explanation: The answer is faint. David says it plainly: "From the ends of the earth I call out to You whenever my heart is faint." He calls out when his heart is faint, and he says so out loud. That's the part I love, friends.

The answer is the rock higher than himself. David prays, "Lead me to the rock that is higher than I." Think about that one, friends. He's not saying he'll climb up there on his own. He asks to be LED, and I can relate, because I couldn't get out of that junk drawer by myself either.

The answer is refuge. David says, "For You have been my refuge, a tower of strength against the enemy." Look at the words "have been," friends. He's talking about what God has been to him, and that's a refuge.

The answer is forever. David prays, "Let me dwell in Your tent forever…" Not a quick stop, a forever stay. Believe me, friends, after years stuck in the back of a junk drawer, I know a good forever when I hear one.

The answer is True. The very next verse says, "For You have heard my vows, O God…" David asks to dwell in the tent forever, then he says God has heard his vows. He's praying with something behind him, friends, not just hoping.

The answer is that David counts himself among those who fear God. He says God has given him "…the inheritance reserved for those who fear Your name." He places himself in that group. I think that's a humble spot to stand, friends: he's one of the ones who fear God, not a special case.

The answer is to increase the days of his life. The prayer says, "Increase the days of the king’s life…" Then it keeps going with "may his years span many generations." That's a prayer for a LONG life, friends, and I'd sign up for that one with my mustache.
The answer is False. The text says, "May he sit enthroned in God’s presence forever…" No set number of years, just forever. Nobody's counting on a calendar here, friends.

The answer is God's loving devotion and faithfulness. The prayer says, "appoint Your loving devotion and Your faithfulness to guard him." Think of those two as guards standing watch over the king, friends. I'd take that security detail over the back of a dusty junk drawer any day.

The answer is to sing praise and fulfill his vows. David says, "Then I will ever sing praise to Your name and fulfill my vows day by day." Notice the "day by day," friends. A promise like that isn't kept in one big moment, it's kept one ordinary day after another.
